stage_2_story.text_en:
Last summer, David and his family visited London for the first time. Their most exciting day was a trip to the British Museum — one of the most famous landmarks in the world.

At the entrance, they paid the admission fee and each picked up a guidebook. A friendly tour guide named James met them near the main hall. He led them through a stunning heritage exhibition about ancient civilisations, explaining the stories behind each artefact.

The children loved the Egyptian mummies, and David could not stop reading the descriptions on every display. At one point, they found a smaller gallery on the second floor, filled with beautiful Greek sculptures. James explained how these pieces were part of Europe's shared cultural heritage.

The problem was that there was simply too much to see. Their itinerary had planned only two hours in the museum, but they ended up staying for almost four. By the time they reached the Roman monument display, the kids were tired but still amazed.

On the way out, David bought two more guidebooks — one for himself and one as a gift. He smiled and said, 'Next time, we need a whole week just for this museum.'
